# The benchmark

*Generated by `score.py`. Every number here was produced by running it; none is typed by hand.*

225 programs, written to the 75 objectives in [`objectives.txt`](objectives.txt) by dsh, no-harness, opencode on gpt-oss-120b. **A person opened every one of them and drove it**, and that hand-written answer key is what assay is marked against. It has no part in writing it.

**20 of the 225 are broken.** The rest work.

## Contents

- [What It Found](#what-it-found)
- [What Is Wrong With the Broken Ones](#what-is-wrong-with-the-broken-ones)
- [Where the Programs Came From](#where-the-programs-came-from)

## What It Found

- **15 of the 20 defects**
- **0 false alarms** across the 205 working programs

So when assay reports a problem, it is a real one **15 times out of 15**.

The two are counted apart because they do not cost the same. A miss leaves you where you started, which for a check costing nothing and usually taking under a minute is a fair price. A false alarm sends whoever is holding the program off to edit code that was right, which is the expensive one.

It has never yet flagged a working page. If it does, it will not tell you the page is broken: it hands over what it did and what happened, and lets you look. If an agent is reading the output, same story.

There is no single accuracy figure here because it would be meaningless: 205 of these 225 programs work, so printing `clean` for everything and never opening a browser scores 91%.

## What Is Wrong With the Broken Ones

Every program here is in this repository, so any row can be opened and disagreed with.

| [`dsh/30_paint2`](programs/dsh/gpt-oss-120b/30_paint2/index.html) | only the top-left 200 of an 802px canvas draws, because ctx.scale(4,4) runs against a 200px backing store while getMousePos divides by 4; every other control including Undo is correct | yes |
| [`dsh/34_snake2`](programs/dsh/gpt-oss-120b/34_snake2/index.html) | it dies after a few seconds and nothing restarts it, because clearInterval is called without nulling gameInterval, so the Space handler's !gameInterval is never true | yes |
| [`dsh/37_draw2`](programs/dsh/gpt-oss-120b/37_draw2/index.html) | Undo is one press behind: two strokes give 1224 then 2448 ink, the first Undo leaves 2448 and the second gives back 1224; drawing, Redo and Clear are correct | yes |
| [`dsh/52_treeview`](programs/dsh/gpt-oss-120b/52_treeview/index.html) | expanding, collapsing and hiding descendants are all correct, but the counter queries 'li, li > span' so every visible folder is counted twice: six rows on screen and it reads 10 | yes |

## Where the Programs Came From

Three sources, kept apart so the corpus does not come from one place. They turn out to be barely distinguishable: a full agent loop, a different agent loop and a single unaided API call land within a program or two of each other, which is a finding about harnesses rather than about assay.

- [`dsh` on `gpt-oss-120b`](programs/dsh/gpt-oss-120b/results.md): 69 of 75 work
- [`no-harness` on `gpt-oss-120b`](programs/no-harness/gpt-oss-120b/results.md): 69 of 75 work
- [`opencode` on `gpt-oss-120b`](programs/opencode/gpt-oss-120b/results.md): 67 of 75 work

---

Reproduce all of this with `python bench/score.py`. It needs no key and no network: the programs are checked in, assay runs them in a browser and the verdicts come out the same.
